name: Determining Whether an Integer is Even or Odd
description: Construct a program that determines whether an integer is even or odd.

comments.content: We need to read and process the integer that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to define a Scanner object.

We can create a Scanner object using the operator new, as shown in this statement. The System.in object represents the standard input stream, which by default is the keyboard. It tells the java compiler that the input will be provided through keyboard.
We prompt the user to enter an integer.
We need to read the integer that the user enters and store it in a variable. We read the input integer by calling the nextInt() method because this input is an integer.
Note that if the user provides a non-integer number, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., int.
We close the scanner as we do not want to process any input from the user in the rest of the program.

We could determine whether the integer is even or odd by performing one test. This test checks whether the integer is even. If the test fails, then we could conclude that the integer is odd.

We use if statement with the remainder (%) operator to test whether the integer is even. The even integer must be divisible by 2 i.e. when it is divided by 2, there is a zero remainder.
The body of this if statement is executed only if the integer is even, that is the remainder when the integer is divided by 2 is zero. Note that the % operator returns the remainder of the division.
This statement prints that the integer is even. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.

The body of the else statement is executed when the if condition evaluates to false, i.e., when the remainder of the integer divided by 2 is not equal to zero. Otherwise, the body of the else statement is skipped.
This statement prints that the integer is odd. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
